title: Jantar Mantar, Jaipur (Brihat Samrat Yantra)
summary: Jantar Mantar in Jaipur, India, is an astronomical observatory of about twenty large masonry instruments built for Maharajah Jai Singh II. Construction was linked to the plan for his new capital in the late 1720s and culminated in 1734-35, continuing to 1738. Its Brihat Samrat Yantra, a huge sundial, is about 27 metres high.

uncertainty.note: ICOMOS: planned with the new capital in the late 1720s, construction culminated in 1734-35 and continued until 1738; Sky at Night: completed in 1734. The start year is an approximation of "late 1720s". End is the present: the observatory is preserved.

as_recorded.value: Construction work seems to have culminated in 1734-35

where.historical_name: Jaipur observatory of Maharajah Jai Singh II, Jaipur state

footprint.description: The Brihat Samrat Yantra only: a triangular gnomon about 45 m long set on a horizontal sundial, with quadrant scales either side. The rest of the Jaipur observatory is not modelled.

measurements.note: ICOMOS evaluation: "Brihat Samrat Yantra (27m)"; the same document gives the gnomon wall as 22.6 m including 3.5 m below ground, hypotenuse 50.1 m; Sky at Night: 27.5 m

phases.description: Linked to the plan for the new capital in the late 1720s; construction culminated in 1734-35 and continued until 1738 (ICOMOS).
Observatory in use for astronomy; maintained in 1771.
Astronomical activity ended around 1800; a metallurgical furnace pit was dug next to the Great Samrat Yantra and two instruments elsewhere were dismantled for a temple.

importance.justification: ICOMOS calls the Brihat Samrat Yantra probably the largest instrument of its type in the world.
